summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening pain at her G-tube site, persistent despite a recent tube exchange and prior steroid injection. Imaging showed inflammatory changes around the tube without abscess or infection. Pain was initially managed with oxycodone but transitioned to oral hydromorphone (dilaudid) with improved control. A trial of bolus tube feeds was unsuccessful due to hypoglycemia, so she was maintained on continuous feeds. The patient remained stable, afebrile, and hemodynamically normal throughout the stay. She was discharged home on continuous tube feeds (NutriHep at 50 cc/hr), dilaudid for breakthrough pain, and instructions to monitor blood glucose and follow up with her surgeon.
